title: Winter and Choir
premise: Mirabel Thackeray returns to Hollowmere House for a routine appraisal, only to find the house cataloguing them back—rooms rearranging to match memories they never wrote down. Their childhood imaginary friend, Wren, waits on the porch exactly as left behind thirteen years ago, and the town's founders' unfinished ritual demands a final voice before the harvest moon. As Mirabel uncovers that the 'noises' were always the house practicing their name, they must choose between erasing themselves into its choir or singing the counter-verse that frees every voice it has kept—including Wren's.
about_author: Gideon Ashgrove is the pen name of a former rural property assessor who spent a decade cataloguing houses across New England and swears three of them were cataloguing back. They write horror about buildings with opinions and the people stubborn enough to listen.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Arriving at Hollowmere House for a court-ordered appraisal, Mirabel notes wrongnesses in their survey: measurements that differ on second pass, a porch step worn by feet that don't exist. Emotional beat: professional denial cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The imaginary friend from childhood sits waiting, unchanged after thirteen years, greeting them by a nickname no one living uses. Mirabel flees to the car; the engine won't start until they say hello back. Beat: terror braided with unbearable tenderness.

chapters.title: Inventory of Wrong Rooms
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Forced back inside by contract, Mirabel finds a room not on any blueprint containing their own childhood drawings—drawings they don't remember making. Beat: the first suggestion memory itself is unreliable.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, with ledger excerpts in italics. In the county archive, Mirabel finds Hollowmere's founding families recorded a 'choir covenant,' nine names, one line torn out. Beat: scholarly dread replacing personal dread.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Won't Say
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A neighbor, Edith Vane, feeds them pie and warnings in equal measure, mentioning her sister 'who sings at night now.' She stops mid-sentence when the house's windows catch the light. Beat: isolation established.

chapters.title: The Humming Walls
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Overnight in the house to finish the survey, Mirabel hears harmonized humming inside the plaster, matching a lullaby only their mother sang—and their mother never lived here. Beat: the past invading the present.

chapters.title: Wren Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren narrates their long wait on the porch in strange, childlike logic, revealing they cannot cross the threshold and cannot remember being anywhere else. Beat: sympathy deepening; Wren may be a prisoner too.

chapters.title: The Second Measurement
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Every measurement now matches the childhood drawings exactly. The house isn't haunted by the past—it is rebuilding toward it. Beat: realization the house wants something specific from them.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Research reveals eight of the nine founders died within a year of the covenant; the ninth, Aurelia Thackeray, vanished. Mirabel shares the surname. Beat: identity as inheritance, unwelcome.

chapters.title: The Torn Line
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Under raking light, the ledger's torn line reads partially: '...and the tenth voice shall be given freely.' Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose—the ritual needs consent.

chapters.title: Edith's Sister Sings
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel visits the Vane farmhouse and hears Edith's sister through the wall, singing harmonies to songs she couldn't know. Edith begs Mirabel to leave town. Beat: stakes made flesh; this happens to people.

chapters.title: Childhood, Rechecked
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel interrogates their own memories of Wren and finds seams: moments that feel installed rather than remembered. Was Wren ever imaginary? Beat: loyalty to a friend vs. suspicion of its origin.

chapters.title: The Room That Appraises Back
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A new room appears containing an appraisal of Mirabel—every secret, debt, and lie itemized in their own handwriting. Beat: shame; the house knows them completely.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Cross-referencing almanacs, Mirabel learns the ritual must complete on the harvest moon—eleven days away—and every prior attempt ended in a 'choiring.' Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers First
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Fragments return to Wren: standing in a circle of nine adults, being asked to sing, refusing. Wren begins to fear what they agreed to instead. Beat: the imaginary friend's innocence curdles into guilt.

chapters.title: The Basement Choir Loft
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Behind a false wall, Mirabel finds nine chairs facing a tenth empty one, each chair holding something personal—a locket, a tooth, a photograph of young Aurelia Thackeray. Beat: the ritual's physical architecture revealed.

chapters.title: Edith Confesses
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Edith admits her family took the ninth chair's place generations ago; the 'singing' spreads to whoever stays too long near the truth. She gives Mirabel her sister's old hymnal. Beat: ally gained, at cost.

chapters.title: The Hymnal's Counter-Verses
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Marginalia in the hymnal contain a counter-ritual: a song sung against the house, freeing the kept voices but destroying the building and everything in it—including, possibly, Wren. Beat: the central dilemma sharpened.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Sleepless, Mirabel weighs saving Wren (stay silent, join the choir eventually) versus freeing everyone (sing, lose Wren). They realize choosing silence was how the house survived a century. Beat: thematic heart stated plainly.

chapters.title: The House Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The house manifests Aurelia's voice, offering Mirabel restoration: their fragmented memories made whole, their debts erased, if they take the tenth chair freely. Beat: temptation with a real price.

chapters.title: Half-Remembered Mother
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Following the house's bait, Mirabel recovers a true memory: their mother once stood in these rooms, humming, before leaving and taking the memory of why with her. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Porch Refuses Them
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel tries to leave town entirely; roads loop back to Hollowmere. The appraisal contract in their bag now bears their signature they don't recall giving. Beat: trap closed; agency under siege.

chapters.title: Edith Taken
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Edith disappears overnight; her kitchen holds two teacups still warm. Her sister's singing has stopped—which is worse. Beat: cost of hesitation made brutal.

chapters.title: Into the Ledger's Blank Page
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren crosses the threshold for the first time in thirteen years—the house permits it now, feeding on proximity to the choice. Wren searches for Aurelia's traces. Beat: Wren's agency awakening.

chapters.title: Aurelia's Room
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren finds Aurelia Thackeray's hidden writing: she didn't vanish; she refused to sing and was 'kept'—become part of the house's harmony. The tenth chair was built for her descendant. Beat: lineage of refusal.

chapters.title: The Choir Auditions
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. That night every wall sings Mirabel's own voice back at them, rehearsing. The house is practicing their part. Beat: body horror of identity—the self performed without permission.

chapters.title: Three Days to Moonrise
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel and Wren compare findings and finally speak honestly: Wren admits they may be Aurelia's kept fragment wearing a child's shape. Loyalty survives the truth—or does it? Beat: relationship tested at its root.

chapters.title: The Counter-Song Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Using the hymnal, Mirabel learns the counter-verses, but each practice makes the house retaliate—cold spots, teeth in doorframes, Wren flickering like a bad signal. Beat: preparation under punishment.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Gave Freely
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel discovers the signature on the contract matches one from childhood: they signed something here at age seven, the night Wren appeared. The friendship itself may have been the price already paid. Beat: devastating reframe of the central bond.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren, learning they were the payment, chooses anyway: they will stand beside Mirabel at moonrise, even if the counter-song unmakes them. 'Better true and gone than kept and lying.' Beat: love proven over self-preservation.

chapters.title: One Day to Moonrise
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Final preparations; Mirabel writes letters—to Edith, to no one—that the house keeps eating. They hide the hymnal inside their coat lining. Beat: quiet before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The house drops all pretense: walls breathe, rooms migrate, the nine chairs scrape into position on their own. Somewhere below, eight voices warm up. Beat: siege atmosphere, dread at maximum.

chapters.title: Moonrise
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The harvest moon rises red. The house opens the basement stair it never had, and the choir begins without them—Edith's voice among them, newly kept. Beat: point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: The Tenth Chair
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. In the choir loft, the house offers everything again—mother, memory, wholeness—as Mirabel stands before the chair. For one terrible moment they want it. Beat: climax of temptation.

chapters.title: Refusal, Sung
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Instead of sitting, Mirabel begins the counter-song. The house screams in nine-part harmony; the loft tears itself apart trying to drown them out. Beat: climax erupts.

chapters.title: Wren's Verse
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren joins the song—their voice, the fragment of Aurelia, completing the melody only a kept voice can sing. Wren unravels note by note, smiling. Beat: sacrifice as the arc's emotional peak.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The house collapses inward, releasing decades of voices upward like birds. Mirabel drags Edith out as the foundation swallows the chairs. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Measured Honestly
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Weeks later, Mirabel files a final report listing the house as 'unimprovable, demolished.' Edith's sister wakes silent and free. Mirabel grieves Wren without regret. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: The Porch Step
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. On the empty lot, Mirabel finds one thing unburned: the porch step, worn by small feet, and chalked on it, a child's drawing of two figures holding hands. Beat: mourning transmuted into evidence of love.

chapters.title: Coda: What Sings Now
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Driving away, Mirabel hums—not the house's lullaby, but the counter-song, keeping it alive by choice rather than captivity. Somewhere faint, a second voice joins for one bar. Beat: open-ended grace; memory as chosen inheritance.
